items.title: CVE-2026-59310: VMware vCenter Directory Traversal (CVSS 9.8) Under Active China-Nexus APT Exploitation
items.summary: A critical directory-traversal vulnerability in Broadcom VMware vCenter (CVE-2026-59310, CVSS 9.8) is being actively exploited by a suspected China-nexus APT. Attackers deploy a reverse SSH framework for persistent access, with campaign activity traced to 361 unique IPs across 47 countries and the largest cluster of compromises observed in Germany.
items.why: vCenter runs the control plane for enterprise virtualization; a CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated traversal exploited by a state actor is a top-tier priority. Patch immediately and hunt for reverse-SSH persistence and anomalous vCenter service account activity.

items.title: CVE-2026-63520: SharePoint Chained Unauth RCE Exploited in the Wild, Added to CISA KEV
items.summary: CVE-2026-63520, a high-severity RCE in Microsoft SharePoint, is being actively exploited when chained with a second flaw to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution against internet-facing SharePoint servers. CISA has ordered federal agencies to prioritize patching alongside newly KEV-listed TrueConf Server vulnerabilities.
items.why: Repeat of the ToolShell/SharePoint pattern of chained pre-auth RCE against a widely deployed collaboration platform. Any internet-exposed SharePoint deployment should be considered at imminent risk of compromise until patched and IR-verified.

items.title: Operation CameraSwarm: 14,530+ Dahua IP Cameras Hijacked via Credential Attacks, Auth Bypass, and P2P Relays
items.summary: Researchers uncovered Operation CameraSwarm, in which threat actors compromised more than 14,530 Dahua-branded IP cameras worldwide by combining credential stuffing, authentication-bypass vulnerabilities, and abuse of Dahua's P2P relay protocol to reach devices behind NAT and firewalls.
items.why: IoT surveillance botnets are ideal covert infrastructure — attackers gain video/audio access, a launchpad inside enterprise perimeters, and DDoS capacity. Any organization running Dahua or OEM-rebranded cameras should audit exposure, isolate devices, and rotate credentials.

items.title: SpyNote RAT + 'WindRelay' Second-Stage Payload in Live Voice-Phishing Campaign Against Bank Customers
items.summary: A new Android campaign uses SpyNote RAT delivered via live voice-phishing calls: attackers impersonate bank employees, walk victims through installing SpyNote during the call, then deploy a second-stage payload dubbed WindRelay for persistent remote access and overlay-based credential capture.
items.why: Combining social engineering with RAT deployment sidesteps store defenses and MFA. Financial-sector defenders should push customer awareness on unsolicited 'bank employee' install requests and monitor for SpyNote/WindRelay indicators.

items.title: Sandbox Escape in isolated-vm: Critical Flaw Breaks the 2,900-Star Node.js Isolation Library
items.summary: Researchers disclosed a critical sandbox-escape vulnerability in isolated-vm, a widely used open-source Node.js isolation library with 2,900+ GitHub stars and 190 forks. Successful exploitation lets an attacker break out of the isolated V8 context and execute code in the host Node process — a full defense bypass for any product relying on it for untrusted-code execution.
items.why: isolated-vm underpins many multi-tenant SaaS platforms, LLM tool-execution sandboxes, and function-as-a-service runtimes. A confirmed escape technique invalidates a common security assumption and demands urgent upgrades plus review of any product embedding untrusted JavaScript.
